prompt:
Use case: sketch-to-render / illustration-story.
Create a NEW COMPOSITION of Tesoro, one continuous transparent four-hex adventure-map asset.
Input 1: TECHNICAL COMPOSITION PLAN. Follow its spatial arrangement and its wide staggered four-lobed OUTER footprint closely. Cream is the allowed artwork area; dark blue outside is forbidden and must be transparent. All schematic blocks are ONLY layout hints. Input 2: prior Tesoro painting is STYLE, craftsmanship, cool timber/warm hull palette and world-detail reference ONLY. DO NOT copy its rigid arrangement, diagonal façade, rows of identical hulls, repetitive basement boxes or matching sail rollers.
PRIMARY CHANGES:
- Reverse the composition: snowy steep cliff/peak and small partly hidden lighthouse in UPPER LEFT, several raised town platforms sweeping behind ships across the upper right, ending in the two-storey GATEWAY TAVERN at LOWER RIGHT. A compact steep rocky stair and rope ladder at that right end go up to the tavern. The only way on to town passes through the tavern and exits to its rear bridge. At opposite end city meets the cliff, snowy path curls around peak to lighthouse peeking from far side.
- BOTH LOWER HEX LOBES must be ALMOST ENTIRELY FILLED with a heavy dense chaotic carpet of ships, edge to edge apart from a modest soft safe margin. Especially fill the LOWER LEFT lobe and the bottom tips of BOTH lobes. No vacant sea patches inside that mass. Fill the gaps in the sketch with additional packed hulls, overlapping decks, chains and connecting planks. Make 25–35 varied weathered pirate vessels, from little sloops to broad merchant ships, wedge-shaped bows, narrow sterns and bulky hulls. They are chained at wildly differing angles: stern-on, bow-on, side-on, oblique, crossed against neighbours. Truly jumbled improvised pirate anchorage, not a disciplined fleet. Warm chestnut, walnut, reddish and copper-brown hulls with individual weathering. Rigging tangled across vessels, masts of visibly different heights and tilts, some missing yards, unequal furled sails. Few narrow turquoise water seams and little broken foam only.
- SAILS are FURLED but NATURAL and IRREGULAR: bundles of ivory, muted cream, patched ochre and grey canvas tied to some yards at different heights and angles, some half hidden by rigging, some short and lumpy, some spars completely bare, a few fore-and-aft sails tied to booms. Avoid identical white horizontal rods and rows of uniformly spaced rolls. No repeating barcode of white sails. No large open deployed sails.
- UNDER-PLATFORM ROOMS: at most THREE irregular extensions attached to different buildings at different levels. One wide low plank room, one narrow crooked lean-to and a small side room, asymmetrical and partly hidden. Most spaces between tall trestles are open shadow and structural crossbracing, NOT a row of lantern cages or identical little boxes.
Town construction: several uneven raised timber platforms at different levels linked by sagging suspension bridges, irregular widths, setbacks and building heights. Cool weathered silver-grey and muted blue-grey building wood and piles, warm lit windows, colorful red/ochre/teal roofs. Lived-in, improvised, richly detailed painterly pirate city. Do not build a perfectly straight uniform boardwalk with repeated support bays.
FRAMING/FOOTPRINT: Fill the plan's four lobes with substantive cliff/town/ships while retaining the upper central notch and left-side inset. Lower row is shifted RIGHT relative to upper row. Keep all meaningful pixels inside the cream silhouette. Natural feathered edge follows individual bows, timber, rocks and foliage; no chopped-off hulls, straight diagonal guillotine edge, polygonal island base, abrupt rectangular cutoff or clipped scaffolding. Entire coherent scene must be visible, with short complete natural ends. DO NOT solve by shrinking the whole motif in an otherwise empty rectangular canvas. The lower two lobes must be a BROAD almost solid ship mass, not a thin line of boats along a diagonal.
STYLE: match the reference's colorful, sculptural, finely detailed watercolor adventure-book painting and oblique aerial perspective, enough distinct big shapes at small map scale and lovely details in enlargement. Organic and hand built rather than a regimented toy model.
Output high-resolution, same 856:680 canvas aspect ratio. TRUE RGBA transparent background. No blue/cream guide colors, geometric outlines, hex lines, words, labels, letters, watermark, border, sky or background sea rectangle. No large navigable open water. The technical sketch is guidance, never part of final artwork.
